title: Financial Planning and Management
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: Financial planning starts with —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Which of the following is a component of financial planning?
questions.answer: A

questions.q: The financial decision concerned with the procurement of funds is —
questions.answer: C

questions.q: It deals with framing of financial policies for procurement, investment and administration of funds to achieve objectives —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Fluctuating working capital is also called —
questions.answer: C

questions.q: Long-term investment decisions are also called —
questions.answer: B

questions.q: The capital structure of an organisation refers to the combination of —
questions.answer: B

questions.q: Current assets are assets that get converted into cash —
questions.answer: B

questions.q: Funds required for purchasing current assets are an example of —
questions.answer: C

questions.q: The ability of a firm to convert an asset into cash is called —
questions.answer: A

questions.answer: B

questions.answer: A

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Identify whether the working capital requirement is high or low: (a) When sales are seasonal. (b) When sales are uniform.
questions.answer: (a) High. (b) Low.

questions.q: (a) What is financial leverage? (b) How is it calculated?
questions.answer: (a) The use of debt in the capital structure to magnify the effect of EBIT on EPS. (b) EBIT / EBT.

questions.q: Identify the financial decisions: (a) Decision relating to long-term investment in fixed assets. (b) Decision relating to short-term investment in current assets.
questions.answer: (a) Capital budgeting decision. (b) Working capital decision.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) Capital structure includes ______ liabilities. (ii) Financial structure includes ______ liabilities and ______ liabilities.
questions.answer: (i) non-current (long-term). (ii) non-current; current.

questions.q: State true or false: (i) Shares are secured. (ii) Debentures are generally unsecured.
questions.answer: (i) False. (ii) False – debentures are generally secured.

questions.q: Give one word for the following: (a) The date on which the board declares a dividend (b) Dividend in the form of bonus shares.
questions.answer: (a) Declaration date. (b) Stock dividend.

questions.q: Differentiate Debt from Equity (any two points).
questions.answer: Debt is borrowed capital, repayable with interest, cheaper and risky; equity is owners' capital, no repayment obligation, costlier and safer for the company.

questions.q: Give an example of current assets.
questions.answer: Cash, inventories, debtors or bills receivable (any one).

questions.q: Give the formula of (a) operating leverage (b) combined leverage.
questions.answer: (a) Contribution / EBIT. (b) Contribution / EBT (financial leverage × operating leverage).

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: State any four objectives of financial management other than maximisation of shareholders' wealth.
questions.answer: Ensuring regular and adequate funds, ensuring optimum use of funds, maintaining liquidity and ensuring safety of investment.

questions.q: Why is wealth maximisation superior to profit maximisation?
questions.answer: It considers risk and the time value of money and focuses on earnings per share, unlike vague profit maximisation.

questions.q: State any two factors affecting the choice of capital structure.
questions.answer: Cash flow position and cost of financing (also tax rate, return on investment and risk).

questions.q: What is the difference between capital structure and financial structure?
questions.answer: Capital structure includes long-term debt and equity; financial structure also includes current liabilities.

questions.q: What is meant by fixed capital? Give an example of its use.
questions.answer: Capital invested in assets lasting more than a year, e.g. buying plant and machinery.

questions.q: Define working capital.
questions.answer: The capital needed for day-to-day operations; the investment in current assets (gross) or current assets minus current liabilities (net).

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: A company is planning to set up a new plant and estimate its future financial requirements. Explain how financial planning will help.
questions.answer: It estimates accurate fund requirements, develops a sound capital structure, ensures proper utilisation of funds, avoids shortage or surplus and helps face unforeseen situations.

questions.q: State any three objectives of financial planning.
questions.answer: To ensure timely availability of funds, to avoid raising excess or inadequate funds and to raise funds at the lowest cost with adequate liquidity.

questions.q: Explain the three financial decisions.
questions.answer: Investment (selecting assets), financing (procuring funds at the best mix) and dividend decisions (how much profit to distribute or retain).

questions.q: Explain the difference between operating leverage and financial leverage.
questions.answer: Operating leverage = contribution/EBIT shows business risk; financial leverage = EBIT/EBT shows financial risk from debt.

questions.q: Distinguish between fixed capital and working capital.
questions.answer: Fixed capital is invested in long-term assets and is used permanently; working capital is invested in current assets for day-to-day needs and circulates.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Discuss the essentials of a sound financial plan.
questions.answer: It should be simple, take a long-term view, be flexible, ensure optimal use of funds, keep the cost of capital low through an optimal capital structure and ensure adequate liquidity.

questions.q: State any five main objectives of financial planning.
questions.answer: Estimating funds correctly, developing a sound capital structure, proper utilisation, avoiding shortage or surplus and controlling financial activities.

questions.q: Explain any five factors that influence fixed capital requirement.
questions.answer: Nature of business, size, scale of operation, technology used, types of products, scope of activities, method of acquiring assets and government subsidy.

questions.q: Explain any five factors affecting the working capital requirement of a business.
questions.answer: Nature of business, scale of operations, business cycle, seasonal factors, production cycle, credit policy, operating efficiency and inflation.

questions.q: Explain the determinants of capital structure.
questions.answer: Cash flow position, return on investment, tax rate, cost of financing, floatation cost, risk, flexibility, control, coverage ratios, regulations and stock market conditions.
